title: Agentforce & Data Cloud

toc.text: 4. Data-space scoping: what an agent may see
5. The full loop: Plan → Ground → Act → Guard

html:
This is the moment the whole roadmap has been building toward. Agentforce — resilient, grounded, autonomous agents — depends on Data 360 for trusted customer context. Data Graphs turn the unified profile into hierarchical JSON an agent can reason over; retrievers and prompt templates ground every answer; data-space scoping decides what an agent may see. This phase is deliberately exam-hands-on, with verified Spring '26 details.

Learning Objectives

By the end of this phase, you will be able to:

  • Explain Data Graphs and why agents query them by IndividualId.
  • Read a Data Graph's hierarchical JSON (Individual → engagements).
  • Choose grounding strategies (retrievers, prompt merge fields, Apex actions, RAG).
  • Apply data-space scoping to control what an agent may see.
  • Place Data 360 in the Agentforce "plan → ground → act → guard" loop.

1. Why agents need Data 360

An agent is only as good as the context it can reach. CRM records give an agent the transaction, not the customer. Data 360 supplies identity-resolved, cross-source context an agent can actually act on:

  • One trusted profile per customer (unify = fewer hallucinated assumptions).
  • Fresh, streamed attributes (churn score, current intent, latest engagement).
  • Groundable, citation-able context (retrievers return the source chunk).
  • Auditable data-space boundaries (the agent's compute is scoped like a user's).

The architecture phrase you will be asked about: "Trusted customer context for Agentforce." Data 360 is the grounding layer; Agentforce is the reasoning/acting layer. The two are bound together by Data Graphs.

2. Data Graphs

A Data Graph is a hierarchical JSON projection of the unified identity. Instead of an agent joining many tables, it fetches a single, nested customer view.

json
{
  "Individual": {
    "IndividualId": "IND-007",
    "Name": "Amina Taylor",
    "LoyaltyTier": "Gold",
    "Predicted_Churn": 0.72,
    "Engagements": {
      "CatalogEngagement": [
        { "ProductId": "SKU-412", "LastViewed": "2026-09-18T14:20:00Z", "ViewedCount": 4 }
      ],
      "CartEngagement": [
        { "CartId": "CART-118", "TotalAmount": 649, "Items": 2, "CreatedDate": "2026-09-17T09:00:00Z" }
      ],
      "AgentEngagement": [
        { "SessionId": "SES-8821", "Topic": "refund", "Status": "open", "LastActive": "2026-09-19T10:12:00Z" }
      ]
    }
  }
}

Where is this JSON used?

  • Agentforce agents access the Data Graph via an Agentforce Data 360 data action and filter — the agent queries by IndividualId and receives the customer's nested context in one hop.
  • Prompt Builder can feed Data Graph nodes into templates as merge fields.
  • Flows can read graph nodes for rich decision inputs.

The rule to memorise: agents look up customers by IndividualId on the Data Graph. That single identifier is the spine of every agentic Data 360 interaction — which is why identity resolution (Phase 4) and unified profiles (Phase 5) are prerequisites: no solid IndividualId, no reliable agent context.

3. Grounding strategies (the "Ground" step)

Every Agentforce answer must be grounded. Data 360 gives you four mechanisms — know when to use each:

MechanismWhat it doesUse when
Data Libraries / RetrieversIndex files/Knowledge; retriever fetches the best chunks (hybrid search)Answers need Knowledge docs, FAQs, PDFs
Prompt Builder merge fieldsInsert Data Graph / profile fields into the templateAnswers need a few known attribute values
Apex actionsRun trusted, governed code (query DMOs, call Data 360) and return JSONAnswers need computation or a live query
RAG on Data 360Semantic retrieval over ingestion + unified contextOpen domain "ask anything" + cite that it returns source chunks

Best-practice snippet (Apex action returning structured context):

apex
@InvocableMethod(label='Get Rewards Context')
public static List<String> getRewardsContext(List<Request> requests) {
    // 1. Resolve the IndividualId (or CRM external key)
    // 2. Fetch the Data Graph / profile attributes via Platform API or mirror Service
    // 3. Return a tight, JSON-serialized context node (limit tokens)
}

Keep the Apex action narrow: return only the fields the agent asked for. Raw tables or giant profiles leak context window (and risk over-exposure).

4. Data-space scoping: what an agent may see

Data spaces are not just analytics isolation — they are agent boundaries:

  1. An agent is scoped to a data space (and to the DMOs/fields in it).
  2. If the customer-success space comprises only service DMOs + a filtered individual view, the agent cannot reach marketing-held data in another space.
  3. Field-level security / permission handling decides which facts within the space an agent can read.

Exam pairing: "How do you guarantee an agent cannot see advertising data?" → build the agent against a data space that does not contain the ad data (least-privilege at the data layer, not just the tool layer).

5. The full loop: Plan → Ground → Act → Guard

text
1. PLAN     Agentforce reasoning/copilot + business prompt
2. GROUND   Data Graph lookup (IndividualId) → retrievers → prompt merge fields → RAG
3. ACT      Apex actions, flows, data actions, CRM updates (Phases 7–10)
4. GUARD    Data-space scoping, permission/field-level security, audit of actions taken

An Agentforce service scenario with Data 360:

  1. Customer asks the billing agent "why is order 5821 refunded?"
  2. Agent grounds by querying the Data Graph for IndividualId (AgentEngagement/Case context) + a retriever on the refund Knowledge base.
  3. It acts via an Apex action or data action to fetch order status.
  4. Guard: Data space only exposes billing/service DMOs; the refund reason must come from retrieved context so the agent doesn't invent it.

6. The Data 360 consultant's Agentforce checklist

  • Unified profiles resolved (IndividualId trustworthy) before agents launch.
  • Data Graph projected over the exact nodes the agents need; hierarchy documented.
  • Data space boundaries defined per agent persona (least-privilege).
  • Grounding mechanisms chosen (retriever vs merge fields vs Apex action vs RAG).
  • Every tool/action auditable; PII masked at the governance layer (Phase 11).
  • The "insufficient context → say so" instruction in every prompt template (Phase 13).

Hands-On Exercises

Exercise 1: Read the graph

For the JSON above, path the fields the agent needs for: (a) "tell me what's in my cart", (b) "when did I last check the sleeve", (c) "what's my churn risk?". Write the JSON paths.

Exercise 2: Grounding choice

For each: (a) warranty answer from PDF; (b) cart total; (c) order-5821 refund reason (order + case + Knowledge). Choose retriever vs merge fields vs Apex action vs RAG and justify.

Exercise 3: Scope it

Design the data-space layout so the service agent can see only service DMOs + a limited individual profile, while marketing agents see marketing DMOs. State which graph nodes exist in each space.

Exercise 4: Build the Apex action

Extend the repo with AgentforceBillingContextService mirroring getRewardsContext above: invocable, single narrow JSON node, guarded Limits.getCallouts(), and a test asserting the returned context contains exactly the requested fields.

Key Terms Glossary

TermDefinition
Data GraphHierarchical JSON projection of the unified profile for agents.
AgentforceSalesforce's agentic AI platform; agents reason and act autonomously.
IndividualIdThe unified identity key agents use to query Data Graphs.
GroundingBinding agent answers to trusted, retrieved context.
RetrieverNo-code config that fetches the relevant grounding chunks.
Data-360 agent actionApex/invocable action or data-action step that fetches Data 360 context.
Data-space scopingLimiting an agent to the DMOs/fields within its data space.
AgentEngagement / CartEngagement / CatalogEngagementData Graph engagement nodes under an Individual.

Certification Checkpoints

  • I can explain why agents query Data Graphs by IndividualId.
  • I can read and design a Data Graph's hierarchical JSON.
  • I can pick the right grounding mechanism (retriever/merge/Apex/RAG) for a scenario.
  • I can apply data-space scoping as the agent boundary.
  • I can trace a grounded agent loop: Plan → Ground → Act → Guard.

Self-Check

  1. Q: How does an Agentforce agent fetch a customer's context? — A: It queries the Data Graph by IndividualId and receives the nested profile (engagements, predictions, attributes) in one hop.
  2. Q: "Answer the refund question from docs, don't invent it." — A: Ground with a retriever over the Knowledge base (hybrid search) and instruct the template to answer only from context.
  3. Q: How do you stop an agent from seeing advertising data? — A: Data-space scoping — build the agent against a data space that does not contain the advertisig DMOs (plus field-level security inside the space).
